concentration_flags: UBER is ~79.48% of NAV -- a single adverse event (the $40M California wrongful-death arbitration award against Uber reported mid-September 2026, broader rideshare-safety litigation wave including a separately settled sexual-assault case with no disclosed terms, the pending Delivery Hero acquisition's integration/financing risk, execution/leverage risk from the EUR4.5B euro bond raise, or intensifying robotaxi competition from Tesla's Cybercab, Waymo, or Uber's own AV-partner strategy) would disproportionately hit the portfolio; cash is effectively nil at ~0.22% of NAV, so there is no cushion against a UBER-specific shock.

trim_considerations.note: Bringing this back to the ~25% single-name guideline would mean reducing exposure by roughly $445.2 -- a consideration, not an instruction, and one that doesn't account for any tax consequences of selling, which this pipeline has no visibility into.
